title: Claims Liaison Memo: Overhead and Profit on Carrier-Funded Reconstruction Change Orders
content:
The markup rate on a Reconstruction change order follows the carrier's overhead and profit practice. The figures it turns on are kept on the insurance claim under Insurance Claim Services: the number of trades on the linked claim file's estimate, and the claim arrangement's minimum number of trades for overhead and profit, overhead percentage and profit percentage.

**Rule.** The change order markup rate is:

- for an insurance-scope or code-required change order on an insurance-claim contract whose linked claim file's estimate carries at least the claim arrangement's minimum number of trades for overhead and profit: the arrangement's overhead percentage plus its profit percentage;
- for an insurance-scope or code-required change order on an insurance-claim contract whose linked claim file's estimate carries fewer trades than that minimum: no markup;
- for every other change order: the tier's change order markup percentage.

## Decision table

| Change order type | Contract funding | Trades on the estimate compared with the arrangement minimum | Markup rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| insurance scope or code required | insurance claim | equal to the minimum | overhead plus profit percentages |
| insurance scope or code required | insurance claim | above the minimum | overhead plus profit percentages |
| insurance scope or code required | insurance claim | below the minimum | none (0%) |
| insurance scope or code required | self-pay | any | tier change order markup percentage |
| owner upgrade or material escalation | any | any | tier change order markup percentage |

## Example (hypothetical arrangement)

Assume a claim arrangement that pays overhead and profit from 3 trades, at 10% overhead and 10% profit. An insurance-scope change order on a claim file whose estimate lists 3 trades is marked up 20%; with 2 trades it carries no markup; an owner upgrade on the same contract takes the agreement's own change order markup percentage.
